title.narrative: Restoration of Wetlands and other important Amazonian Ecosystems - Capacity-building, innovation, development and technological transfer for ecological restoration and climate change mitigation

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project seeks to integrate forest restoration with the livelihoods strategies of local communities and farmers and make the sustainable exploitation of forest resources economically viable through support for the strengthening of the restoration and of non-wood forest products value chains. The theory of change of this project but also of bioeconomy policy and models under development is that this creates significant incentives for the restoration of degraded lands, the implementation of agroforestry models and the sustainable use of natural resources provided by the standing forest and, hence, becomes an important ingredient in strategies to combat the conversion of forests into arable land or pastures, often with much lower economic returns per hectare. Although the project is expected to deliver these benefits at the local level in the conservation units included in its activities, the assumptions on which the project is based have application at the national level and certainly also at the level of the entire Amazon basin. Colombia, for example included bioeconomy, natural ecosystems, sustainable territory in its national development plan as one of five development strategies, with the objective “to promote sustainable territorial development through knowledge, conservation and use of biodiversity and its goods and ecosystem services, considering research and innovation ecosystems as instruments and as an institutional strategic program, innovation and transparency for institutional transformation focused on social and regional convergence”77. Ecuador prepared a white book on bioeconomy78 which defines bioeconomy as “the production of goods and services based on the sustainable use of biological resources and their derivates, including ecosystem services”79 while Brazil launched in 2024 its national bioeconomy strategy with the objective to coordinate and implement public policies with respect to the development of bioeconomy, defined as productive and economic development model based on values of justice, ethics and inclusion, able to generate products, processes and services through the sustainable use, regeneration and conservation of biodiversity, guided by scientific and traditional knowledge and with a view to add value, the generation of jobs and income, sustainability and climate stability80 81. Project activities are aligned with FAO policies on decent employment in forestry, in particular with the goals of “increasing opportunities for entrepreneurship and employment in forestry while avoiding deforestation and forest degradation” and “increasing social dialogue and representation through effective and strong cooperatives, producers’ organizations and forestry workers’ unions82. The strengthening of restoration value chain has the potential to promote employment and decent work for rural people, especially for young people and women. The project will work closely local communities and MSMEs to guarantee good work conditions in all activities related to the project.?In this sense the project will contributes to Decent Rural Employment (DRE) as supported by FAO, as follows: Employment creation and enterprise development Local communities trained in restoration value chain activities, such as seed and seedling production, biodiversity assessment and monitoring. The project will also support the development of seed collection networks and seedling nurseries, articulating with partners to support access to new market. The project will also support local MSMEs in accessing innovative markets in NWFP value chains, increasing income generation, and decent rural employment. Social protection: occupational safety and health measures for the rural workforce adopted by promoting safer technology for restoration and NWFP production; working conditions improved in rural areas, including effective maternity protection and living wages in agriculture. Standards and rights at work: Socially responsible value chains supported, specifically to reduce gender and age based discrimination; Child labor prevention and reduction in rural areas supported by tackling its root causes (poverty, lack of education) and providing livelihood alternatives to poor households; The project will guarantee compliance with national labor legislation promoted in rural areas.??? Governance and Social Dialogue: Countries supported in strengthening democratic organizations and networks of producers and workers, particularly in the in the restoration and NWFP value chains; Representation of the rural poor in social dialogue and policy dialogue through their organizations supported; Participation of rural poor in local decision-making and governance mechanisms supported; Rural women and youth groups empowered to be involved in these process from the initial steps; Synergies built between organizations, projects, and producer-to-producer learning opportunities created.

To restore wetland and lowland forest ecosystems and biodiversity in the Amazon mainland and coast through strengthening people and Local Communities capacity for ecosystem restoration, improving the enabling environment, and initiating restoration in overlooked areas of the Amazon.
